report.source_text: At two-month follow-up, the skin lesions showed significant improvement and the lesions were completely resolved after four months of therapy leaving atrophic scars (Figure 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old male presented with a chronic large verrucous plaque with malodorous purulent discharge on buttocks, thigh, and scrotum, progressing over two years with painful itchy ulcerated nodules and systemic symptoms including untreated cough and night sweats. Initial biopsy showed marked pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and epithelioid granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis and lymphocytic infiltrates. Acid-fast bacilli staining and mycobacterial culture were negative. Despite no microbiological confirmation, the clinical presentation and characteristic histopathology supported the diagnosis of TVC. Clinical improvement and complete resolution of lesions after four months of anti-tuberculous therapy confirmed the diagnosis.
